CONSTITUTION, BY-LAWS, AND UNIVERSITY MANUAL COMMITTEEReport #2022-2023-15 - SECOND READING OF MOTION TO AMEND THE SENATE BY-LAWSFACULTY SENATE, March 23, 2023 Background and contextIn response to the discussion about preferred modalities of Faculty Senate meetings that arose duringthe Senate meeting onOctober 20, 2022and that wasincluded as “Old Business” in the agenda forthe Senate meeting onNovember 17, 2022, CBUM discussedthe issue and with theagenda for theFaculty Senate meeting on December 8, 2022includedfor consideration areportwith a motion toamend the By-Laws of the Faculty Senate to continue to permit the option of remote participation inFaculty Senate meetings.
During theDecember 8, 2022meeting, prior to the presentation of theCBUM report, Senator Preisser moved to eliminate the possibility of remote participation in FacultySenate meetings.
The motion failed.
Subsequently Senate Vice President Nassersharif moved to tablethe CBUM motion to codify the option of remote participation in in-person Senate meetings in theFaculty Senate By-Laws.
A majority of the Senate voted in favor of Vice President Nassersharif’smotion.

In January 2023 CBUM revised the original motion and submitted a new version to FSEC whorequested that the committee draft specific language changes to the By-Laws for consideration by theFaculty Senate.
RationaleIn recognition of the critical role of meaningful faculty engagement in shared governance, CBUMaffirms that it is essential that Faculty Senators,ex officiomembers of the Faculty Senate, andmembers of the General Faculty actively participate in Faculty Senate deliberations and meetings.
Thecommittee further urges that all members of the university community participate in Faculty Senatemeetings in-person whenever possible, as a matter of cohesion and of maximizing opportunities tosupport and nurture our sense of community.

Although the committee urges in-person attendanceand participation whenever possible, in the interests of equity and inclusion and as a means tooptimize our democratic processes by facilitating the broadest level possible of engagement withFaculty Senate business and participation in Faculty Senate deliberations, CBUM invites the FacultySenate to consider amending the By-Laws to codify the option for remote attendance for all in-personFaculty Senate meetings, with community members, Senators, andex officiomembers who attendvirtually retaining all rights afforded to people who are able to attend in-person:- All attendees retain the right to speak and to participate in discussions.- Allex officiomembers of the Faculty Senate retainthe right to make and second motions.- All Senators retain the right to make and second motions, and to vote.
Current language in theBy-Laws of the Faculty Senate:7.3 Regular Faculty Senate Meetings shall be held at least once each month on Thursdays during theacademic year.
